definition: A rule that gives exactly one output for each input in its domain.
The set of input values a function is defined for; in a model, the context can limit it further, for example to times $t \ge 0$.
The set of output values a function takes over its domain; this is not the range of a data set, which is the largest value minus the smallest.
A function or equation that describes a real situation approximately, and is only valid over a domain the context allows.

The function $f^{-1}$ that undoes a one-to-one function $f$: if $f(a) = b$ then $f^{-1}(b) = a$, its graph is the reflection of the graph of $f$ in $y = x$, its domain is the range of $f$, and $f^{-1}(x)$ is not $\frac{1}{f(x)}$.
A function in which no two different inputs give the same output, so every horizontal line meets its graph at most once and the function has an inverse.
